slides.title: Solve this in ==15 seconds== — or you're not ready

slides.stem: If 3x − 7 = 11, what is the value of 6x − 14?
slides.prompt: Time yourself. Comment your time and your answer.

slides.title: C — 22
slides.body: No algebra needed: 6x − 14 is exactly *double* 3x − 7, so the answer is 2 × 11 = 22. Solving for x = 6 and rebuilding gets there too — the slow way. The SAT is betting you'll spend a minute on a ten-second question.

slides.title: Expression questions have a shortcut on purpose
slides.body: When the SAT asks for the value of an *expression* instead of the variable, check whether it's a multiple of what you were given — these questions are written so the fast path skips solving entirely. And x = 6 sits in the choices, waiting for everyone who forgot what was asked.
slides.tip: Before you solve, re-read what they asked for
